multiplication-meaning: write a multiplication expression for a picture or story of equal groups and tell what each factor means.
describe an array with rows and columns and find the total by multiplying.
multiply by 2, 5, and 10 using skip counting and patterns.
solve equal-group, array, and measurement word problems by drawing a model and writing a multiplication equation.
division-meaning: share a total equally among a number of groups and write a division equation for how many are in each group.
make groups of a given size from a total and write a division equation for how many groups there are.
solve a division fact by finding the missing factor in a related multiplication fact and write fact families.
solve sharing and grouping word problems within 100 with a drawing and a division equation.
properties-fact-strategies: use the commutative property to turn an array or fact around and know the product stays the same.
regroup three factors to make multiplying easier and show the product is the same.
break a factor into two easier parts, multiply each part, and add the two products.
explain and use the rules for multiplying by 0 and 1 and dividing by 1 and by the same number.
find any fact to 10 × 10 with a strategy such as doubling, adding a group, or subtracting a group.
addition-subtraction-1000: round a whole number to the nearest 10 by finding the two tens it is between and deciding which is closer.
round a whole number to the nearest 100 by finding the two hundreds it is between and deciding which is closer.
add within 1,000 using place value strategies and the standard algorithm, regrouping when needed.
subtract within 1,000 using place value strategies and the standard algorithm, including across zeros.
round to estimate a sum or difference and decide whether an exact answer is reasonable.
patterns-unknowns-two-step: find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation in any position, such as 8 × ? = 48 or 5 = ? ÷ 3.
write an equation with a symbol for the unknown when the total, the group size, or the number of groups is missing, and solve it.
multiply a one-digit number by a multiple of 10 using place value, such as 4 × 60 = 4 × 6 tens = 24 tens = 240.
describe a pattern in an addition or multiplication table and explain it using properties or even and odd numbers.
write an equation with a letter for the unknown to represent a two-step word problem.
solve two-step word problems with the four operations and use rounding or mental math to check that the answer makes sense.
understanding-fractions: name the unit fraction 1/b for one of b equal parts of a whole and tell whether parts are equal.
explain that a/b is a copies of 1/b and name a fraction shown by a model or a story.
partition the interval from 0 to 1 into b equal parts and locate 1/b on a number line.
locate a/b on a number line by marking off a lengths of 1/b from 0, including fractions greater than 1.
equivalent-comparing-fractions: use fraction bars and number lines to show that two fractions are equivalent because they are the same size or the same point.
write a simple equivalent fraction (halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, eighths) and explain why it is equivalent with a model.
write a whole number as a fraction and recognize fractions such as 6/3 or 4/4 that equal whole numbers.
compare two fractions with the same denominator by comparing numerators, record with >, =, <, and justify with a model.
compare two fractions with the same numerator by reasoning about the size of the pieces and justify with a model.
time-volume-mass: read and write time to the nearest minute on an analog clock and a digital clock.
find a start time, end time, or elapsed time in minutes using a number line or a clock.
read a liquid volume on a scaled container and estimate liquid volumes in liters.
read a mass on a scale, choose grams or kilograms, and estimate the mass of everyday objects.
add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems with masses or liquid volumes in the same units.
graphs-measurement-data: use the key of a scaled picture graph, including half symbols, to find and compare amounts.
read a scaled bar graph, including bars that end between grid lines, and solve one- and two-step how many more and how many less problems.
choose a scale and draw a scaled picture graph or bar graph that matches a data table.
measure lengths to the nearest half inch and quarter inch with a ruler.
make a line plot of measurement data marked in whole numbers, halves, or fourths and answer questions about it.
area: explain that area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape with no gaps or overlaps.
find area by counting unit squares and name it in square centimeters, square meters, square inches, square feet, or square units.
find the area of a rectangle by tiling and show that multiplying the side lengths gives the same area.
split a rectangle with side lengths a and b + c into two rectangles and show that its area is a × b + a × c.
find the area of a rectilinear figure by splitting it into rectangles that do not overlap and adding their areas.
perimeter-shapes: find the perimeter of a polygon by adding all of its side lengths, including sides that are not labeled.
find an unknown side length when I know the perimeter and the other side lengths.
draw and compare rectangles that have the same perimeter and different areas, or the same area and different perimeters.
sort shapes by their attributes and explain that rhombuses, rectangles, and squares are all quadrilaterals.
partition a shape into parts with equal area and name the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
